summary: On Hyperliquid perp charts: tap a candle to see which wallets traded in it, and see where tracked wallets' liquidation prices and stop orders sit on the chart.
overview: Wallet Intel shows who moved a Hyperliquid candle. Tap or click any candle and a panel lists the wallets that traded in it: how much each one bought and sold, at what average price, and its share of the candle's volume. The panel also shows the candle's totals and how much of the volume came from market buys versus market sells.

On the chart it draws liquidation clusters as bubbles (red for longs, green for shorts, bigger for more dollars) and stop and take-profit trigger orders as short bars from the price axis. Tap one to see the wallets behind it. Tap any wallet for its profile: account value, open positions with entry and liquidation price, and its full address with a copy button and a link to the public explorer. In the Book panel on a Hyperliquid chart, tapping a price row lists the tracked wallets with orders at that price.
how: Every public Hyperliquid trade names its buyer's and seller's wallet. TradeZoro's server reads every trade on every perp, adds them up per wallet per minute and keeps 7 days, so the candle view covers every wallet that traded, not a sample. Wallet names come only from public sources: the wallet's own name on the public leaderboard or a public vault's name. Everyone else is shown as a short address.

Liquidation prices, stop orders and resting book orders are only public wallet by wallet, so the server follows a set of the largest wallets (the top of the public leaderboard by account value and by 30-day volume, plus wallets seen making large trades) and reads them every few minutes. The panel says how many wallets that is and what share of open interest they hold, for example "tracking 280 of the biggest wallets ≈ 15% of open interest". Liquidations, stops and book orders of other wallets are not shown.
use: Tap a large candle to see whether one or two wallets did most of its volume or whether it was spread across many.
Some traders watch where large liquidation clusters sit relative to the current price.
Use it to check which tracked wallets have stop or take-profit orders near a level.
Tap a price in the Book panel to see whether a large resting order belongs to a tracked wallet.
notes: Hyperliquid perps only. On other symbols the indicator shows a short note instead.
Free for everyone, including signed-out visitors.
Candle wallets are kept for 7 days. Clusters and book orders are read every few minutes; the chart says when they were last updated (for example "updated 4 min ago").
Liquidation prices move as prices, margin and positions change. A cluster shows where tracked positions would be liquidated now, not that they will be.
Nothing is drawn in bar replay.
